steps.text: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C). Lightly grease a 7x11-inch baking dish.

Mix flour, salt, and pepper in a shallow dish. Place beaten egg in another shallow dish. Combine bread crumbs, Parmesan, sage, and lemon zest in a third shallow dish. Gently press a pork chop into flour mixture to coat, then shake off excess flour. Dip into beaten egg, then press into bread crumbs. Gently toss between your hands so any bread crumbs that haven't stuck can fall away. Place breaded pork chop onto a plate while breading the remaining pork chop; do not stack.
Heat olive oil and butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Brown pork chops for about 4 minutes per side, then transfer to the prepared baking dish.
Bake in the preheated oven until no longer pink in the center, 10 to 15 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 145 degrees F (63 degrees C),

raw_recipe.headline: Parmesan Sage Pork Chops
raw_recipe.description: Crusted with bread crumbs, lemon zest, Parmesan, and sage, these pork chops are seared before they're baked for a crunchy coating that's perfection.
raw_recipe.name: Parmesan Sage Pork Chops

review.reviewBody: This is a solid recipe. I made these using a cast iron skillet - sear one side, flip and then the skillet goes into the 425 oven. Only cook to about 145 though and then allow to rest. "USDA recommends cooking all whole cuts of meat to 145 °F as measured with a food thermometer placed in the thickest part of the meat, then allowing the meat to rest for three minutes before carving or consuming."

Thanks to the person who recommended using a cast iron skillet- what a difference! So much crispier than when I have used a regular baking pan. I did not have a lemon on hand this time so I added 1/2 tsp of lemon pepper seasoning in the flour and just omitted the regular pepper. Also added a bit to the bread crumbs. Only used 1/2 cup of bread crumbs with the fresh parm and sage, and still had a lot left over even after coating 3 big chops. Cooked on iron skillet til well browned on one side, flipped them, and put skillet in a 375 oven for 15 minutes. (Lower temp to avoid smoking up the house. ) Liked this recipe before; loved it this time!

DELICIOUS!! I did have to alter the recipe to accommodate my Ketogenic way of eating and my husband’s Gluten Free Sensitivity— I omitted the flour and Breadcrumbs but used the Delicious seasonings with my Parmesan and Egg! The Flavor is still having a dance party in my mouth ! Oh- I also hammered out the pork and squeezed some of the lemon juice from my zested lemon on the pork then sprinkled with Parmesan cheese, dipped in egg and then rolled it in the Parmesan cheese/ lemon zest and sage mixture! It was extremely helpful to have a Delicious concept that I was able to tweak!!

This recipe was excellent. I took the advice of another reviewer and used a cast iron skillet and put that in the oven. If you use a convection oven, the cook time is shorter. I had bone-in 1 inch chops and they took 10 minutes oven time.

Very good and moist! I didn't have Italian Breadcrumbs so I used plain and added Italian Seasoning and Garlic Powder. I also used a cast iron pan as others suggested and didn't have a rack that fit so instead, I took 2/3 of my 'naked' lemon and sliced it into 4ths as I had 4 pork chops before putting them in the oven (set to 375 as some others suggested), I slide a slice of lemon underneath each to keep the chops out of the fat and add a little more flavor, which also caused caused a crust on both sides. I also added a more of the Parmesan mixture on top, a little too much, next time I will use less. I cooked them for about 20 minutes but mine were boneless and about an inch thick. I cooked them until they were about 145 and then let them rest as I cooked the asparagus and finished up the noodles. I took the last of the lemon (sliced and cut in quarters) and added it to the water (brought the water and lemon to a boil first) I was using to cook the asparagus. Also served some rotelle noodles tossed with garlic infused olive oil, a bit of butter and grated Parmesan cheese. Kids loved it, even the picky boy! Yes, a very cohesive meal and may be too boring for some but the boy prefers his flavors "match, not fight". As you can guess, its a challenge to find a meal he likes.
The chops had a wonderful lemony flavor and not overly greasy, with using the lemon slices in cooking, I will add more Sage next time.
Easy. Delicious! I double dipped in the egg mixture and the panko. Amazing crust! Juicy!

I was looking for a recipe for boneless pork chops that was different from the usual. THIS was one of the best recipes I have had in a very long time. I changed it minutely by using parmesan - Romano cheese. I also used garlic pepper and garlic salt. I took the advice of a reviewer and put the chops on a rack over a sheet pan to keep them nice and crispy and lowered the temp to 375. like I said small changes but the basic recipe will be my go to from now on! Thank you for taking a boring meal and changing it into an awesome dinner!

Great recipe and delicious. Definite keeper. I used fresh sage and freshly grated Parmesan cheese along with panko bread crumbs since I had all on hand. I used a case iron skillet and after flipping the porks chops over immediately put pan in the oven for 10 to 15 minutes. Came out perfect. Otherwise followed recipe as written .

Very nice. I removed it from the skillet to cool on a plate. Then drained the skillet, added a little chicken broth to deglaze the pan. Once it reduced by half, I added a splash of lemon juice and whisked in two tablespoons of butter and drizzled it over each chop after platting.

4.5 stars. I enjoyed the lemon peel and sage combination. I finished the chops in the pan, I didn't transfer to the oven and they turned out fine. I used fresh sage and deglazed the pan with a little white wine. The only change I would make is to use less bread crumbs and Parmesan, there was too much and it was a waste of ingredients (and I made 3 large chops). I plan to make this recipe again.

we used regular thickness pork chops. I had to add a tablespoon of egg whites because one egg wasn't enough and a bit more flour. My daughter declared that there wasn't enough lemon rind, so we used about a tablespoon of freshly grated lemon rind. the extra lemon really brought out the flavor of the cheese. yummy. 5 stars with the extra lemon.

I have made these many times, and they always turn out awesome. I substituted Italian seasoned panko crumbs for bread crumbs (needed about 2/3 cup for 2 large chops), and it raised it to the next level! 5 stars is all I can give it though. ;>)

Really liked the flavor. They were crunchy on the outside but juicy on the inside. I had 4 small to med boneless chops. The only thing I changed was I used 1/4 tsp dried lemon peel instead of zest, repeated the egg and breadcrumb step to give them a little extra coating since there was quite a bit left over. Still had plenty loftover so as others said could cut back on amount of the breadcrumb mix. Cooked them 375 for 25 min. Came out perfect

I've made this multiple times. Very good recipe. I'll give you a little extra goodness....I'd use the pan I browned and cooked it in, add a little garlic, some butter, (cook garlic in butter slightly)add cream, a little splash of white cooking wine, and black pepper. Use it as a little sauce over chops.
Awesome recipe. Used small, thick cuts and turned out so juicy and tender, very flavorful!
Outstanding recipe! No changes needed! Will be in the rotation for sure!
Fantastic! They were tender and delicious!
Excellent!
These were a hit!!! I took Jillian’s advice and did 375 instead of 425, and I did 25 mins instead of 15. Sooooo tender and juicy! I also did 3 mins searing on each side instead of 4.
The chops were crispy and tasty. I didn't have lemon zest so I did without. I will save this recipe for anytime I want breaded, baked chops. Absolutely yummy and moist. Great recipe.
